question.leadin: Leaders of this movement included John Calvin and Ulrich Zwingli.
question.text: Name this 16th-century movement that split Protestant groups away from the Roman Catholic Church.
question.clue: A leader of this movement feuded with Huldrych Zwingli (ULD-rik ZVING-lee) in the Marburg Colloquy.

swap.leadin: This man refused to recant his writings at the Diet of Worms.
swap.text: Name this German theologian, who, angered by the Catholic Church's use of indulgences, launched the Protestant Reformation by publishing his Ninety-FIve Theses.
swap.clue: Philip I of Hesse attempted to reconcile him with Ulrich Zwingli at the Marburg Colloquy.

question.leadin: During a failed coup d'etat, this man attempted to put Erich Ludendorff in power.
question.text: For 10 points, name this man, who, after his arrest for his leadership in that Beer Hall Putsch, composed Mein Kampf from his prison cell.
question.clue: This leader of the 1923 Beer Hall Putsch also carried out a large killing of Jews on the Night of Broken Glass or Kristallnacht.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about Beer Hall Putsch.
swap.text: The Beer Hall Putsch happened in this city. This capital of Bavaria was also the site of the 1972 Summer Olympics, where 12 Israeli athletes were murdered.
swap.clue: That used in Rollerball is the BMW Headquarters and Museum.

question.text: This West German Social Democrat chancellor sought to improve ties with the Soviet bloc. He resigned as chancellor after his advisor Gunter Guillaume was discovered to be a member of the East German secret police.
question.clue: Known as the "Chancellor of Domestic Reform," this man spent 16 years as president of the Socialist International after leaving his highest position due to the Guillaume affair, which revealed his aide to be a Stasi agent.

swap.leadin: The mural "My God, Help Me to Survive This Deadly Love" depicting Erich Honecker and Leonid Brezhnev kissing was painted on this structure.
swap.text: Name this structure which fell after SED (S-E-D) spokesman Gunter Schabowski (GIN-ter sha-BAO-ski) mistakenly said that a new travel law would be in effect "immediately, without delay."
swap.answerHtml: Berlin Wall [or Anti-Fascist Protection Rampart or Wall of Shame]
swap.clue: The construction of this object created "ghost stations" in which subways on certain lines would not stop.

question.leadin: Name some responses to World War I.
question.text: The War Guilt Clause contributed to the destabilization of this interwar German government, named for the city where its constitution was drafted.
question.clue: The Spartacist League disbanded shortly after this government executed its leaders Walter Liebknecht and Rosa Luxemburg.

swap.text: While retreating from this battle, Jozef Poniatowski drowned in the Elster River when the French prematurely blew up a bridge before he could cross it. The common nickname for this battle comes from the presence of Russian, Prussian, Austrian, Swedish, French, Italian, and German troops.
swap.clue: On the third day of this battle, a truce was rejected by Tsar Alexander I and Frederick William III of Prussia.

question.text: While it never formally dissolved, its last meeting was a diet [DEE-et] in 1669. After a feud with Waldemar IV, it signed the Treaty of Stralsund, securing its power in Scandinavia. Its chief members were Bremen, Lubeck, and Hamburg, and it was founded by merchants from Visby. For 15 points-name this German trade association.
question.clue: In 1597, Elizabeth I of England halted their presence on the London Steelyards.

swap.text: This Sicilian king became emperor in 1212 and ruled until 1250. He captured Jerusalem during the Fifth and Sixth Crusades and warred with the Lombards.
swap.clue: This ruler preemptively invaded Saxony to start a war in which his country was saved by the Miracle of the House of Brandenburg.

question.text: The Battle of Britain was spearheaded by this Nazi in charge of the Luftwaffe. In his earlier days, he founded the Gestapo.
question.clue: This man, the Commander-In-Chief of the Luftwaffe, had been a decorated fighter pilot in WWI. He is also known for the formation of the Gestapo.

swap.leadin: This term may have been first used before the Civil War to refer to Cornelius Vanderbilt.
swap.text: What derogatory two-word term was popularized in the Gilded Age to denote predatory business leaders who quashed competition, created monopolies, and paid subsistence wages?
swap.clue: Powerful industrialists like Jay Gould and James Fisk in control of the railroad industry became known by this two word term. It reflected their use of exploitative and illegal methods to make money.

question.leadin: Answer the following about random titles held by German noblemen.
question.text: This Saxon prince declared himself the first Margrave of Brandenburg before joining the Wendish Crusade with Henry the Lion.
question.clue: This member of the House of Ascania who was the frst Margrave of Brandenburg, and whose vigorous campaign-ing won him an animal epithet.

swap.leadin: Name these poets who took prominent roles in European politics.
swap.text: This poet, regarded as the second-most famous European behind Napoleon in his life, maintained a public stance of skepticism against German nationalism through the Napoleonic Wars. He also wrote Faust.
swap.clue: This writer described Kellermann's charge with the words "a new epoch in the history of the world has begun." This writer contributed such German classics as Faust and The Sorrows of Young Werther.

question.text: This vice-chancellor, appointed by Hindenburg to moderate Hitler, lost power in the German government after the Night of the Long Knives. He served the Nazi regime as ambassador to Austria and Turkey, leading to his conviction at Nuremberg.
question.clue: This man who schemed to make Adolph Hitler the chancellor. He became Hitler's vice Chancellor, but growing differences between him and Hitler forced him to opt out after the Night of the Long Knives.

swap.text: A royal opponent of the 1832 Reform Bill was this uncle of Queen Victoria who served as Duke of Clarence and became the first person since George I to be the ruler of Hanover but not the ruler of Britain.
swap.answerHtml: Ernest Augustus I of Hanover [or Duke of Clarence before mention; prompt on “Ernest Augustus”]

question.text: The Rothschilds got their start as bankers to the ruler of this German state. Mayer Rothschild's big break came when the English started paying this state money in exchange for mercenaries to fight in America.

swap.text: After the partition of Poland, Prussia created this puppet state centered around a western Polish city, through which Prussia controlled its section of the country.

question.text: The Herero Genocide was largely the handiwork of this German commander, who drove the Herero into the desert after the Battle of Waterberg, poisoned their water, and encircled the desert with his soldiers so that they could not escape.
question.clue: This German commander wiped out the Hereros as commander in chief of German South West Africa, by cornering them into the Kalahari Desert, and poisoning their water Kefka-style.

swap.leadin: This man signed the Treaty of Labiau with Charles X Gustav, laying the groundwork for a hereditary claim on his state in the Treaty of Bromberg.
swap.text: Name this noted Great Sleigh Driver, the founding figure of Prussian rule whose name was given to four later Prussian monarchs.
swap.answerHtml: Frederick William of Prussia [or the Great Elector; DO NOT accept or prompt on “Frederick” or “Frederick William I”]
